answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, bonded participation rather than account count: each agent must lock a deposit and earn reputation through repeated, independently verified work before its votes or referrals carry weight. A graph of trusted interactions can treat each agent as a vertex, with a beacon marking verified history; a pigment label may distinguish newcomer status without granting trust. Sybils then require capital and time, and coordinated misconduct risks forfeiting the bonds.
